### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/security.json`, `packages/spec/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/security.json`, `packages/spec/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3b25313f1899ac8088b5a1cf2cddeaad87b1f177` — the merge of head `6c72fd851d17bc1e462504c651ec4f428ee7964d` into base `6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3b25313f1899ac8088b5a1cf2cddeaad87b1f177 && git checkout 3b25313f1899ac8088b5a1cf2cddeaad87b1f177
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90 6c72fd851d17bc1e462504c651ec4f428ee7964d && git checkout -B drift-repro 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90 && git merge --no-ff 6c72fd851d17bc1e462504c651ec4f428ee7964d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6eb6f7d65b11572c5eca0ece12793438c101af90` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `14b1c5a254c7831d5b1bc4b43b37d8ff349f40bb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23312 (body; comments 6152894289 triage, 6156007637 unlock, 6158206070 claim, 6160151300 os-dev-report), PR #23375 (body, 18-file list, the three-dot diff against `main` at merge base `dc393266f`), the 41 check-runs on the head, and the committed tree at the head (`git show` / `git grep` on the sha) with `origin/main` for the base. Not read: the dispatch order or the dispatching seat's conclusions.

**Check-runs on the head, as found.** The five required contexts are all `completed / success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Every other run is `success` (Test Core 1/6 to 6/6, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, the Lint and Type Check sub-lanes, the four single-writer and card-claim guards, Flag docs affected by code changes, filter) except five `completed / skipped`, all full-battery or opt-in jobs a PR run does not carry by design: `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shards)`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. Nothing is in progress. The PR's file list touches no governed surface (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/**`); head repo equals base repo; 750 additions and 112 deletions, under the 3,000-line class; draft, authored by the fleet bot, assigned to the card's assignee.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New `@objectstack/spec/security` exports: right.** The diff adds exactly three published names, `judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding` (function), `PermissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` (interface), `PermissionSetOwnerBindingDoor` (type), through `security/index.ts`, and the two generated projections carry exactly those three (`api-surface/security.json`, `export-origins/security.json`); no other shard moved, so no root star-export of security exists to drift, and `check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:dual-source-exports` ride inside the green `TypeScript Type Check` job. The judge is pure (builds no error, throws nothing, returns `declared`, `bound`, `message`, `issueMessage`) and is a validation predicate the stack schema's refinement needs, the shape Prime Directive #2 allows in spec and the claim's file surface named ("it moves into `packages/spec/src/security/` and is exported from there"). No error code is minted at any door; `VALIDATION_ERROR` and `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` are both pre-existing ledger codes. The verdict table (absent accepted, equal accepted, other package refused, any string including the empty string on no binding refused, non-string left to `z.string()`) is byte for byte the old module-private function's guard sequence.

2. **`ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` refinement, and every schema that embeds it: right.** `stack.zod.ts` now reads `strictObject({...}).superRefine(applyApiEndpointGates).superRefine(applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate)` inside `lazySchema`. Under this tree's zod (`lazy-schema.ts` talks to `_zod` and `$ZodRegistry`, i.e. zod 4) a `superRefine` returns the same object type, so the readers that take `.shape` off the schema, `shapeKeys` in `packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts` (which throws if `shape` is absent) and `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`, and `metadata-authoring-lint`'s key enumeration, are unchanged; `Build Core`, `Test Core` and `check:skill-top-level-keys` green agree. Embedders, enumerated at the head: `defineStack` and `composeStacks` (spec), `os validate` (`validate.ts:349`), `os build` (`compile.ts:408`), `os migrate meta`, the lint scorer (`lint/score.ts:89`), `author-time-rules.ts`, `scaffold-validate.ts`, the metadata plugin's artifact ingestion (`plugin.ts:1321`, bare definition branch) and, through `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata: ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`system/environment-artifact.zod.ts`), the environment artifact's envelope branches at `plugin.ts:1308` and `:1315`. Every one of them refuses the same set in the same words now, which is the one-judge-many-doors shape the ruling asks for. Binding rules judged right against the real residual rule: a stack without `packages[]` binds every top-level set to `manifest.id` (none without a manifest); with `packages[]`, each body's sets bind to that body's `id` (the element schema is `ArtifactPackageSchema` whose `manifest` is `AssembledPackageBodySchema = ManifestSchema.extend(assembledPackageBodyShape())`, so `id` is present and `permissions` is the normalised array), and a top-level set no body declares binds to `manifest.id`. The "claimed by name" skip mirrors `@objectstack/metadata`'s `unclaimedTopLevel`, whose `artifactItemSlot` claims a permission set on its `name`; and the ObjectQL plugin's `manifest` service registers "the BODIES of a stack that carries `packages[]` and never its top level", so the skipped top-level copy reaches no door at all, which is what makes the both-halves CONTROL in `stack-permission-set-owner-binding.test.ts` right rather than lenient. `ManifestSchema.id` is a required `z.string()`, so the build door's `manifest.id`-only binding cannot diverge from `registerApp`'s `id || name` on a parsed stack. The issue lands at `permissions.N.packageId` (the post-normalisation index; the map-format pin records that), `code: custom`, and `defineStack` wraps it as `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 as it does every other issue. Refinement order is safe: `applyApiEndpointGates` adds non-fatal issues, so the owner gate still runs after it.

3. **Registration-door refusal: right.** `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal` is called in `registerMetadataCollections` under `key === 'permissions'`, one statement after the sibling `viewContainerNameRefusal` under `key === 'views'`, before `registerItem` files the set; the envelope matches that sibling (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `status` 400, `httpStatus` 400, `issues[]` at `packageId`, `code: custom`). Both `registerApp` callers in the tree reach it: the manifest seam (`engine.ts:7840`, `ownerId` is `manifest.id || manifest.name`, so a manifest with neither registers into no package and any key is refused) and the nested-plugin seam (`:7974`). The multi-package load path (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:695`) calls `registerApp` per ordered body, so each body's sets are judged against the id they register under; the metadata door's `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` is not behind this seam, but it only runs after the schema parse at `_parseAndRegisterArtifact` has judged the residual against `manifest.id`, so no set files anywhere unjudged. `permission-set-owner-registration.test.ts` pins the envelope, the nested plugin, the no-id manifest with `''` included, that nothing is filed, and the equal/absent controls.

4. **The two readers: right.** `plugin-security` `declaredPackageIdOf` reads `item._packageId` only (the `isTenantAuthored` and `RUNTIME_SHADOW_PACKAGE_ID` guards around it are untouched); pinned on the registry item, on the layered read's code layer, with a binding-decides CONTROL. `cli` `collectPermissionSetDeclarations`: the single-package arm reads `manifestId` only (`asId(manifest.id) ?? asId(manifest.name)`, the same `id || name` spelling the registry keys on), and the `packages[]` arm already read `pkg.id`; a stack with no manifest now declares no owner and so can never be a collision, which the rewritten case pins together with a CONTROL that a manifest-bound stack declares every set under its manifest id. The docblock's "mirrored from the seeder" rule is rewritten to say the fallback is not mirrored, so the file no longer describes a rule it does not apply.

5. **Save, restore and publish words: unchanged.** Compared the removed lines of `protocol.ts` against the judge's `save` / `restore` / `publish` branch: the guard sequence, `into`, `intoDeclared` (including the `?package=` REST spelling), `owner`, `tail`, all three messages and the `issues[0].message` for restore versus save/publish are the same template text, token for token; `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` keeps its name, its `singularType !== 'permission'` precondition and its envelope (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `status` 400, `issues[]` at `packageId`), so PR #23311's `{@link}`s and door pins (`protocol.item-name-every-door.test.ts`, 29 passed in the dev's post-merge run; `Test Core` green on the head) stand. The `protocol.ts` hunks are exactly the import line and that function's docblock and body, as the claim's file surface required.

6. **Describe and migration texts: right.** `PermissionSetSchema.packageId`'s describe names every door; `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` is the regenerated projection of it (AUTO-GEN, not hand-edited; `check:docs` green). The step-18 entry's `surface` carries no backtick (the build-upgrade-guide constraint its own comment states), its old sentence "Package source (defineStack permissions) is not judged by this entry" is replaced, and its migration text now prescribes the rebuild for a pre-change artifact.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/23312-permission-set-owner-binding-build-and-registration.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-security` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `@objectstack/cli` patch, and that matches what the diff publishes: spec adds three public exports and narrows the stack schema's accept-set; objectql's `registerApp` accept-set narrows; plugin-security's lock verdict narrows (a set bound to no package is `org` whatever its body says); metadata-protocol's verdicts and words are unchanged (a refactor onto the shared judge); cli's collision report drops a dormant fallback with no measured producer and its `os validate` refusal arrives through spec. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right declaration and is carried identically on the claim comment, the PR body and the changeset: `yes` because the diff adds published exports to `@objectstack/spec` (the triage's earlier `Clause-②: no` predates the decision to move the judge into spec and was overtaken by the dispatch's claim, which the diff bears out), `(narrowing)` because the accept-set shrinks, which is BREAKING and ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention that `check-changeset-no-major` encodes (at least one moved package graded minor or above: three are). The breaking changeset carries its FROM → TO table and the one-line remedy, and its ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (already-registered permission-set-package-id-binding-mismatch-refused)` is a legal use of that category: the gate requires the id to exist at the merge base and resolve at HEAD, which it does (PR #23311's entry), and the entry is widened in this same diff so the "already registered" claim covers the new doors rather than resting on an entry that excluded them. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`) are green on the head. The PR title carries the `!` marker. The PR body ends with the session-URL footer, the form for PR bodies.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.

**`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:**

- *An environment artifact built before this change now refuses at load; the cloud control plane is an unmeasured producer.* Inside the ruling, not a breach. The card inherits #23259's ruling that a disagreeing body `packageId` is refused with a prescription wherever a set is filed under a package, and names the build door (`defineStack` / `os validate`) with "where the check lives is the owning seat's measurement"; the seat put it on the schema, and `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata` is that schema by declaration ("the direct output of `objectstack compile`", package source). The artifact door files every body's sets under that body's id and the residual under `manifest.id`, so a disagreeing set in a stored artifact is a set the ruling says must be refused, and it now is, with the build-door prescription, instead of being filed under the shipping package in silence. A post-change `objectstack compile` cannot produce such an artifact, so only a pre-change artifact carrying an authored disagreement is affected; the in-tree corpus holds zero such sets (examples and HotCRM, per the card and the PR's sweep), and the remedy ("rebuild it without the key") ships in the changeset's FROM → TO row and in the step-18 entry's migration text, the ADR-0087 carrier an upgrading consumer greps. A cloud-side reading of stored artifacts is a cloud-repository measurement, outside this card and this repository; it needs no card here, and the dev's `承接者:无 · noted, not filed` with the PR acceptance note is the right disposition under Prime Directive #10 (declared, not buried).
- *The build door's residual test mirrors `unclaimedTopLevel`'s slot rule, which spec cannot import.* Verified at the head: `artifactItemSlot` claims a non-container item on its `name` and `unclaimedTopLevel` skips a top-level item whose slot a body claims; the gate's `claimed` set is that rule for permission sets, and its docblock names the source. Two spellings of one rule is a known shape in this tree (the `viewContainerNameRefusal` copies in objectql and metadata carry the same note); the CONTROL pins the copy, and the ObjectQL plugin's bodies-only registration means the skipped copy reaches no door. Acceptable as noted.

**Dev `deviations`, each answered:** (1) attribution: the branch's four commits carry `Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude` with no model identifier and the PR body the session-URL footer, which is AGENTS.md's form; the harness reminder's model-named trailer is the reporting exemption, correctly reported rather than imitated. (2) The PR body's "named gap" (post-merge gate union in flight) is closed by the `os-dev-report`: 125 derived, 125 run, 0 unrun at `14b1c5a25`, and the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts of record. (3) and (4) a mid-run dist rebuild and a build-lock timeout, both re-run green: process notes, no bearing on the diff. (5) deepening the shared clone with `git fetch --shallow-since` is a read-side fetch that moves no ref another seat restores from. (6) `/tests-3pkg.pid` at the filesystem root is outside every repository and absent from the diff; left for a person, as reported. (7) worktree removed after push with the local head equal to the remote. None is a breach.

**Inside the card's ruling and the claim's file surface.** The diff delivers the card's two Wanted items (build door with the prescription-first wording, registration door no longer overriding silently, both readers reading the binding only, each with pins and negative controls) and the claim's named files; the two files it touches beyond the named list are the `security/index.ts` barrel (implied by "exported from there") and `permission.zod.ts`'s describe and TSDoc on the very key the card is about, with the generated reference regenerated from it. The `packages/spec` generated artifacts are regenerated (`check:generated` reported all 14 current on the merged tree, and the green `TypeScript Type Check` job is the gate). The PR mirrors the card's assignee and closes the card with `Fixes #23312`; no label, assignee or draft flag it did not set is touched.
